newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares jump 3.35pct in strong volume.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares jump 3.35pct in strong volume.

text.p: The Greek bourse settled 3.35 percent higher on Friday, adding on to Thursday's gains and market watchers said lower interest rates was the main driving force.

"The bourse rose after the central bank's recent changes in money market operations. Investors are expecting a further drop in all interest rates," said investment analyst John Haveles, at Delphi Mutual Funds.
The Bank of Greece has announced major changes in its money market operations. It will institute regular weekly repo and depo volume or interest rate tenders to influence short-term rates.
Market sentiment is positive as there are expectations of more aggressive cuts by Greek banks in their savings accounts and lending rates, he said.
"It is obvious that banks are ready to invest in riskier investment alternatives than they used to. One of these vneues is bonds and I expect their prices to shoot up soon," he added.

Greek equities will benefit form the virtuous circle of falling inflation and interest rates and the stock market will resume its uptrend this year, Carnegie International said in its March research report.
"This report reinforces the market's optimism. Foreign investors are gradually starting to put their money in Greek equties," he said.
Another assistant fund manager said he expected the rise in the bourse to be milder than the one in January.

"The market should rise mildy, between 1.0 to 3.0 percent daily. I do believe that this year will be a positive year for the Greek bourse," said John Glykos, an assistant fund manager at Doriki Mutual Funds.

The Athens general share index settled 3.35 percent or 43.39 points higher at 1,338.76 points from Thursday's 1,295.37 close after opening at 1,311.56. Turnover rose to 17.0 billion drachmas on volume of 4.3 million shares.
Advancers led decliners 183 to 44, with 24 issues unchanged on 251 traded.

Construction shares led the advance, closing 4.57 percent higher. Banks rose 4.13 percent. Industrial shares closed 3.14 percent up and investment shares gained 1.61 percent. Small caps ended up 1.72 percent.
